answer: Each identity binds a carrier SIM: the protocol sends a challenge from the epoch beacon to the number, and the registrant must return a SIM-toolkit signature in one hour. Carrier KYC makes each SIM cost an ID check plus about $2 to $10, so K fake identities cost K times that friction, and carriers flag bulk activations. The protocol cross-checks batches: many SIMs from the same inlet shop or the same IMEI ridge in a day are queued for review and slashed if fake. Limits: lax SIM registration, dual-SIM phones, and eSIM farms lower the bar, so pair SIM binding with liveness checks and slashing.
